founded: 1990 (began operations as Bank Dhofar Al Omani Al Fransi; later renamed BankDhofar. FSA register shows establishment date 14 Jan 1990)

Abdul Hafidh Al Ojaili and his companies 24.99%, Dhofar International Development & Investment Holding Co SAOG 23.30%, Social Protection Fund 10.75%, Yousuf bin Alawi bin Abdullah and his companies 9.76%, and Sheikh Mustahail Ahmed Al-Ma'ashani and his companies 7.45%; others 23.75%. government_link: Partly. The Social Protection Fund holds 10.75% (31 Dec 2025, S2). The June 2026 presentation says 'Government & Omani Protection funds' own c.28% of share capital and cites high probability of government support given systemic importance (S3). The FSA register (undated) also lists the Civil Service Pension Fund 10.07% and Ministry of Defense Pension Fund 5.25% (S14). The largest holders are private (the chairman's group and a listed holding company).
group_structure: Single listed bank with a domestic Islamic banking window, Dhofar Islamic (formerly Maisarah Islamic Banking services; allocated capital OMR 70m; 31 Islamic branches at 30 Jun 2026) (S1 note 1, S2 note 1). No subsidiaries are disclosed in the statements opened. Asset management, corporate financial advisory and proprietary investment sit in the Investment Banking division (S2 p.48). The bank acquired the assets and liabilities of Bank of Baroda's Oman branch on 1 Apr 2025 (S2 note 1.2).
footprint: Oman only. 145 branches at 30 Jun 2026 (114 conventional and 31 Islamic), 353 ATMs, 188 CDM/CCDMs and 5 multi-function kiosks, with 12% market share in assets, loans and deposits (S1 note 1, S3 slides 6, 8).
customer_segments: Retail mass, Ladies and Youth lifestyle propositions, Al Riadah Priority (affluent), Al Rifaa Privilege, Private Banking (HNW/UHNW, launched June 2024), Numo SME, corporate, government and GREs, Islamic (Dhofar Islamic), and NRI customers added with the Bank of Baroda Oman integration.
business_lines: Segments in the June 2026 presentation: Retail Banking, Corporate Banking, Treasury/Investments/Financial Institutions, and Dhofar Islamic (revenue split 24/40/17/19 per the investor presentation). Retail includes Al Riadah, Al Rifaa, Private Banking and Retail Wealth Management (the last two set up in June 2024). Investment Banking has three departments: Asset Management, Corporate Financial Advisory and Proprietary Investment (S2 p.48, p.53).

capabilities.wealth_summary: BankDhofar built its wealth franchise recently: Private Banking and Retail Wealth Management were both launched in June 2024. The affluent tiers are Al Riadah Priority (salary of 3,000, savings balance of 30,000 or fixed deposit of 250,000 as published, currency not stated) and Al Rifaa Privilege. Private Banking asks for an investment portfolio of at least 400,000 and offers onshore and offshore planning, offshore booking centres in Switzerland, Singapore and the UAE, structured products, alternatives (private credit and equity, hedge funds, real estate, precious metals), a multi-broker and independent-custody model, and asset-backed lending through partners. Retail wealth starts from OMR 1,000 and covers mutual funds, bonds and sukuk and model portfolios built with BlackRock. BlackRock was announced as a partner on 13 Oct 2025, described as the first arrangement of its kind in Oman. In-house Asset Management runs a Money Market Fund, a Shariah-compliant GCC Equity Fund and discretionary Portfolio Management Services. Total AUM is not published; fiduciary discretionary funds were OMR 70.09m at 31 Dec 2025. The website describes no digital wealth platform, and the next-generation mobile app was in pilot in H1 2026.

segments.name: Private Banking
segments.eligibility: Clients must be able to establish an investment portfolio of at least 400,000 (or local currency equivalent); currency not stated. Targets HNW and UHNW individuals, family businesses, corporates and government entities.

private_banking.detail: Private Banking officially launched June 2024 for HNW and UHNW clients, with dedicated relationship managers, investment advisors and product specialists. Services: wealth and business succession planning, trust, foundation and family office structuring, onshore and offshore investing, offshore booking centres in Switzerland, Singapore and the UAE, consolidated global custody, asset-backed lending through partners, metal cards. No head of private banking is named in the sources opened.

asset_management.detail: BankDhofar Asset Management sits in the Investment Banking division (with Corporate Financial Advisory and Proprietary Investment); not a separate legal entity. Funds: Bank Dhofar Money Market Fund (minimum 1,000, daily liquidity, prospectus Nov 2025), Bank Dhofar GCC Equity Fund (Shariah compliant), plus Portfolio Management Services in fixed income, equity and real estate. FSA register activities: Investment Manager, Portfolio Management, Fund Administration, Issue Management, Investment Advice & Research, Marketing non-Omani Securities. AUM not disclosed. Clients: institutions, UHNW and retail.

brokerage.detail: The FSA register lists no Brokerage activity for Bank Dhofar (S14). The private wealth page describes a 'multi-broker approach and independent custody for equities and bonds' without naming brokers or a custodian (S8). No MSX brokerage arm is mentioned in the annual report.

digital_investing.detail: The website describes no digital wealth platform or in-app investing (S7, S15). Digital onboarding runs through the Intilaqa app. The H1 2026 board report says the bank entered the pilot phase of a next-generation mobile banking application with 'expanded service capabilities'; no investment features are described (S1).

advisory.detail: Relationship managers assess risk tolerance and goals and recommend products; ongoing advice, market insights and portfolio reviews are offered (S7, S8). The bank holds an FSA 'Investment Advice & Research' activity (S14).

discretionary.detail: Portfolio Management Services with customised strategies by goals, risk tolerance and horizon, across fixed income, equity and real estate; no minimum stated (S9). Fiduciary note: OMR 70.09m of funds managed under Discretionary Portfolio Management at 31 Dec 2025 (S2). FSA Portfolio Management activity (S14).

model_portfolios_robo.detail: Model Portfolios 'built with BlackRock' are listed in the retail wealth offer in the FY2025 annual report, and the chairman's message says the BlackRock partnership gave customers 'first-of-its-kind model portfolios' (S2 p.9, p.53). The 13 Oct 2025 announcement describes a globally diversified portfolio across asset classes and customised strategies but does not mention model portfolios by name (S13). No robo-advice found.

funds_platform.detail: Private wealth page: access to 'over 150,000 funds', including Shariah-compliant mutual funds and ETFs. Retail wealth offers mutual funds, bonds and sukuk. The platform or fund distribution provider is not named.

structured_products.detail: Private wealth page lists structured products with capital protection and enhanced yields. Issuers not named.

private_markets.detail: Alternatives listed on the private wealth page: hedge funds, private credit and equity, real estate and precious metals, with asset-backed lending through external partners. Managers not named.

islamic_wealth.detail: Bank Dhofar GCC Equity Fund (Shariah compliant) with minimum 1,000 (S9); Shariah-compliant mutual funds, ETFs and sukuk through private wealth (S8); Dhofar Islamic advertises 'Integrated Islamic Wealth Solutions' (S3). Dhofar Islamic Wakala funds under management were OMR 9.7m at 31 Dec 2025 (S2). Dhofar Islamic has 113K customers and its own Shariah Supervisory Board of five scholars (S3, S2 p.310).

partners.what: Global investment strategies, diversified portfolios and advisory for HNW, affluent and corporate clients; model portfolios built with BlackRock per the annual report. Described as the first such arrangement in Oman.

partners.what: Three-phase modernisation completed in 2021: Finacle 11 core banking, treasury and payments, Finacle Online Banking (retail and corporate), Finacle Digital Engagement Hub, and over 1,100 RESTful APIs; no wealth module named. The bank's 2026 materials describe a further consolidation of conventional and Islamic cores.

Completed acquisition of the assets and liabilities of Bank of Baroda's Oman branch (business transfer agreement dated 27 Jan 2025), adding NRI customers
Announced partnership with BlackRock to offer global investment strategies and wealth solutions to HNW, affluent and corporate clients

H1 2026: pilot phase of a next-generation mobile banking application, merchant portal for acquiring customers, POS Financing and SME service desks

opportunities: Retail Wealth Management only started in June 2024 and lists funds, bonds/sukuk and BlackRock-built model portfolios from OMR 1,000, yet the website describes no digital wealth platform or in-app investing (S2 p.53, S7, S15).

The H1 2026 board report says a next-generation mobile app entered pilot, and the Q2 2026 presentation describes a unified Digital Hub and a consolidated conventional and Islamic core, which creates a build window for embedded wealth (S1, S3 slide 15).

Dhofar Islamic (113K customers, financing +21%, deposits +14%) advertises Integrated Islamic Wealth Solutions, while only one named Shariah fund (GCC Equity) appears on the asset management page (S3, S9).
Private Banking lists private credit, private equity, hedge funds and real estate via partners, with no managers named, so the alternatives shelf appears to be arranged externally (S8).
The bank has shown willingness to take a named global partner for wealth products (BlackRock, Oct 2025) and treats partnerships as a transformation pillar (S13, S3 slide 15).
barriers: BlackRock is already the named model-portfolio partner (S2 p.53, S13), so a model-portfolio or managed-solution pitch competes with an incumbent.
In-house Asset Management holds six FSA activities and runs its own money market, Shariah equity and discretionary offers (S9, S14).

No FSA brokerage or custody licence; the bank relies on unnamed brokers and custodians ('multi-broker approach and independent custody'), so any execution capability would be sourced externally (S14, S8).

The CEO seat is held on an acting basis, the Dhofar Islamic report says the bank is changing its core banking system, and the 2021 Finacle estate exposes 1,100+ APIs, so integration choices are tied to a platform change in progress (S5, S2 p.250, S20).

Infosys Finacle: core, treasury, payments, online banking and Digital Engagement Hub with 1,100+ APIs, completed 2021; no wealth module named (S20)
Unnamed multi-broker and independent custodian for equities and bonds (S8)
MetLife: strategic alliance listed in the investor presentation, scope unclear (S3)

open_items: Lead check: 'Maisarah Islamic window' is the former name. The FY2025 annual report says the window is 'Dhofar Islamic (formerly Maisarah Islamic Banking services)' (S2 note 1). The rebrand date was not found; the annual report's Basel text still says 'Maisarah entity' in one place.

Lead check: relationship with Ubhar Capital is not supported. No Bank Dhofar shareholding in Ubhar Capital or joint deal was found in the annual report, the FSA register or search results, consistent with om-ubhar.json (owners are Jabreen Capital/OMINVEST and Arab Bank (Switzerland)). The only link is indirect: OMINVEST (Ubhar's controlling group) led a rival 2023 bid for Ahli Bank against Bank Dhofar (S16).

Merger check 2024-2026: no merger involving Bank Dhofar was found other than the completed acquisition of Bank of Baroda's Oman branch (1 Apr 2025). In 2023 Bank Dhofar proposed to merge with Ahli Bank (rejected by Ahli's board, April 2023; S19) and then made a takeover offer in May 2023 against a competing OMINVEST-led offer (S16); neither is recorded as completed and Ahli Bank still files its own results (see om-ahlibank). The July 2026 Bank Nizwa proposal to buy Alizz Islamic Bank from Oman Arab Bank does not involve Bank Dhofar.

The date Gopakumar became Acting CEO and the reason are not in official sources opened. A third-party profile (Simply Wall St, not cited) gives 5 Sep 2024. Check MSX disclosures for the announcement and any permanent CEO appointment.

No named head of Private Banking, Retail Wealth Management or Asset Management was found. The live page lists only 11 chief officers; the annual report names Dhofar Islamic heads (two included as Requires verification).
BlackRock partnership: which BlackRock products, platform and technology are used, and the start date for clients, are not published. The announcement states no minimum or eligibility.
Al Rifaa Privilege eligibility, and the currency of the Al Riadah and Private Banking thresholds, are not stated on the pages opened (OMR is likely but not confirmed).
Q3 2026 results were not published on the IR page on 12 Oct 2026. Re-check late October.
LinkedIn search for the Acting CEO returned no matching profile; other people were not checked.
Ticker BKDB is taken from the IR page's link to the MSX snapshot; the MSX page itself showed no news items.
